title: 9B CPU-only vs CPU+GPU tandem: two controlled runs at 24,576
command: KINDI_DEVICE=cpu python -m kindi --pack ~/.kindi/packs/bonsai-9b --ctx 24576 bench --split-at none --json cpu.json; python -m kindi --pack ~/.kindi/packs/bonsai-9b --ctx 24576 bench --tandem cpu-first --tandem-cpu-layers 6 --sample-vram --split-at none --json tandem.json; then the same pair again into cpu-2.json and tandem-2.json (one fresh process per placement)
notes: This is the controlled replacement for the old cross-run 9B tandem-to-CPU ratio. The 2B/4B rows remain one pair; the 9B row is the median of two fresh-process pairs because run 2 was 23-38% slower on the CPU side. The shallow ratio is 3.0x in run 1 and 4.1x in run 2, so the two-run median is 3.5x; the 3.0x reading is not stable. Run 1 verified 4/4 and 133/133 at both placements; run 2 was throughput only. The full-GPU 9B rows remain the 2026-11-17 capacity run, and no thermal control was applied.
